ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The working principle of the electromagnetic railgun is that the projectile to be launched can move freely between two parallel rails and maintain good contact with the rails. Current flows in from one rail, passes through the conductive projectile, and then flows back through the other rail. The rail current generates a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the rails at the projectile (which can be considered as a uniform magnetic field). The electrified projectile is then propelled at high speed along the rails due to the Lorentz force acting on it. Xiao Ming purchased a railgun model online, with a rail length of \( L = 0.5 \, \mathrm{m} \), a parallel rail spacing of \( d = 0.02 \, \mathrm{m} \), a projectile mass of \( m = 0.02 \, \mathrm{kg} \), a rail current of \( I = 10 \, \mathrm{A} \), and a magnetic field strength of \( B = 1 \, \mathrm{T} \). All resistances are neglected.

1. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the projectile moving along the trajectory?
2. What is the magnitude of the projectile's exit velocity?
3. What is the power of the electromagnetic railgun when the projectile is launched?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are upper and lower two horizontal parallel rails, and a gray vertical conducting rod/projectile is connected across between the two rails; the current arrow on the lower rail points to the right, passes upward through the vertical projectile, and then returns to the left from the upper rail. On the right side of the projectile there is a horizontal arrow pointing to the right, indicating that the projectile is subjected to force/moves to the right along the rails, and the figure is also labeled "parallel rails". Reasoning: The projectile is a conducting rod spanning the spacing between the two rails, so the effective current length under force in the magnetic field is the rail spacing d. Given in the problem L = 0.5 m, d = 0.02 m, m = 0.02 kg, I = 10 A, B = 1 T. The magnitude of the Lorentz force F = BId = 1 × 10 × 0.02 = 0.2 N. The acceleration a = F/m = 0.2/0.02 = 10 m/s^2. If starting from rest and the force is constant, it undergoes uniformly accelerated motion within the rail length L, and the exit speed v = sqrt(2aL) = sqrt(2 × 10 × 0.5) = sqrt(10) m/s. According to the method, take the instantaneous mechanical power at launch/at the exit as P = Fv = 0.2sqrt(10) = sqrt(10)/5 W.
